narration: Welcome to the Harappan Civilization gallery. Here we have the famous Dancing Girl, accession number NM 49.34/1, a bronze figure cast by the lost‑wax method that dates to about 2500 BCE. The 10.5‑centimetre tall, nude woman stands with one hand on her hip and the other arm adorned in bangles, her hair in a thick braid, offering a rare glimpse of informal posture from the Indus Valley. It was discovered in 1926 at Mohenjo‑daro by Ernest Mackay and became part of the National Museum’s holdings in 1949 after the Archaeological Survey of India transferred its Mohenjo‑daro collection. This piece is one of the earliest known bronze sculptures in the world and a testament to the sophisticated metallurgy and artistic life of the Harappan people.
